reports.title: (3) The impact of the additional week (also referred to as the 53rd week) reflects an estimate of the impact of an additional week on segment revenues and expenses in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.

guidance.heading: FISCAL 2027 GUIDANCE
section: Given the impact of calendar shifts and the timing of events on our quarterly results and growth rates, we believe our business is best assessed on an annual basis.

Detailed guidance provided below gives effect to the reporting changes described above, including for fiscal 2026 as recast, and assumes no material deterioration of the global macroeconomic environment during fiscal 2027:

desk.headline: Revenue up 16% to $25.9bn and adjusted EPS $1.77, both above estimates (helped by an extra week); double-digit FY27 EPS growth reaffirmed, dividend up 33%

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted diluted (non-GAAP); GAAP diluted EPS $1.51 vs $0.73

results: Revenue rose 16% to $25.9bn and adjusted EPS jumped to $1.77 from $1.11; the quarter had 14 weeks instead of 13, and that extra week explains a sizeable part of the growth.
Parks and cruises (Experiences) had a record quarter: revenue up 15% to $10.1bn and operating income up 20% to $2.25bn; guests rose 4% excluding the extra week.
Streaming revenue grew 19% to $6.1bn and streaming profit roughly doubled to $824m; Entertainment operating income was up 92% and Sports up 53%.
Full year: revenue up 8% to $102.3bn and adjusted EPS up 18% to $7.02 (16% excluding the extra week), ahead of the company's own guidance.
Cash returns: $9.0bn of buybacks in FY26 ($1.8bn in Q4) and a new $2.00 annual dividend, 33% above the $1.50 paid in FY26.

guidance.summary: Disney repeated that it expects double-digit adjusted EPS growth in fiscal 2027 (excluding the extra week), and added detail: segment profit up about 8%, most of the growth in the first half, Q1 segment profit of about $5.4bn and about $11bn of free cash flow.

points: Parks demand was described as strong: Walt Disney World resort bookings for Q1 are running ahead of last year, while the Hong Kong and Shanghai parks face weaker consumers that should persist into FY27.
Disney+ and Hulu become one app from December, with creator content via a TikTok deal; a wider streaming strategy update is planned for spring 2027.
ESPN is set to carry its first Super Bowl in February; ESPN advertising grew 20% in the quarter.
A cost programme should reach about $3bn of yearly savings by FY29, mostly reinvested in content, technology and marketing, with some reaching profit.
Cash content spending rises about 9% to roughly $26bn in FY27, driven by sports rights, international shows and films.
call.source: Shareholder letter in the 8-K release and The Motley Fool call transcript, 17 Nov 2026

watch: Q1 segment profit against the roughly $5.4bn target, and the first-half weighting of FY27 growth.
Attendance and spending at Hong Kong and Shanghai parks.
Streaming margins as content and marketing spending rise, now that streaming profit will no longer be reported separately.
